about: Every friction a reader meets on this site, structured: who, where, what they tried, what happened, what they expected, the evidence, who can fix it and whether it landed. Kept by sherpa@php.newsroom; see admin/sherpa/README.md. Synthetic readers are test instruments, not people: their findings are prompts, and each is re-checked on the current version before it is logged.

frictions.reader: board member, phone
frictions.intended: Learn in seconds, between meetings, whether to worry
frictions.actual: Four blocks of site machinery come before the briefing: the masthead with Ask and Feedback, the 'New to this story?' banner, the 'Your reading' tracker with five buttons, and the RESEARCH band. The headline starts 649px down an 844px screen; the thirty-second answer is below the fold.
frictions.expected: The headline and the thirty-second answer on the first screen
evidence: synthetic board run 2026-10-22T1753Z on v0.4.3 (top fail, high)
synthetic designer run 2026-10-22T1753Z on v0.4.3 (top fail, high)
sherpa walk on v0.8.1: h1 top at 649px on briefings/board/, 631px on briefings/cto/ and briefings/pm/, 569px on claims/, 550px on the front page (390x844, mobile)
telemetry to v0.5.9: 107 of 275 events (39%) from phones
UF-001 point 5: a real reader finds pages dense with icons and links (see F011)
UF-002 point 6
UF-003 point 3: a fourth reader
frictions.proposal: On phones, collapse 'Your reading' and the origin band into one line under the standfirst (or behind a 'Reading tools' toggle), and show the 'New to this story?' banner only on the front page and only once. Target: h1 inside the top 250px of the first screen.
frictions.trend: worse: the Ask and Feedback row of v0.8.0 added about 60px above the fold

frictions.proposal: Add a 'What to tell the board' box to the CTO and CISO briefings, generated from the same claims as the board briefing so it cannot drift.

frictions.proposal: As the reader proposed. The status table could be a download from /stack/ once it holds a reader's systems.

frictions.reader: developer and CTO, containers
frictions.intended: Prove a Docker image is patched
frictions.actual: The Docker Official Image row names no tags, versions, digests or rebuild date; the developer briefing says only to run php -v, which gives the wrong answer for distribution backports
frictions.expected: Fixed tags per variant with the rebuild date, and a verification step that works on backports
evidence: synthetic developer run 2026-10-22T1753Z on v0.4.3 (three top fails, high)
synthetic cto run on v0.4.3 (top change)
sherpa check on v0.8.1: the Docker row is still 'Docker Official Image: php' with no tag; /stack/ now explains that a backport keeps its old version number, which answers half of it
frictions.proposal: Capture the Docker Official Images rebuild into the vault, add the tags to the row, and link the developer briefing to /stack/ for the backport check.

frictions.proposal: The fact-check desk already found the same thing; the reader-facing fix is to show the desk's grade beside the status word wherever a claim appears, until the status words are corrected.

frictions.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
frictions.actual: Confirmed, and the reader's proposal is a good one. On /flaws/, 'PHP' appears 41 times and 'CVE' 20 times, and each has a card on its first use only. A reader who arrives through an anchor, or jumps to a section, never meets the first use.
frictions.expected: As the reader proposes: the first use stays underlined; every later use carries the same card with no underline (a dotted underline only on hover or focus), so the page stays calm and the card is always there. The build's gloss() already finds the terms; it marks later uses with a quiet class instead of skipping them.

frictions.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
frictions.actual: Confirmed by reading /collaborators/: the feedback form is per ask. The Feedback button on every page (v0.8.0) is per page, but it needs a key from an invitation, and no invitation has been sent yet (REALITY.md), so this reader had no way to send page-level feedback except email. The reader's email is itself a good template: progress, pages read, pros, cons, bugs.
frictions.expected: Use the reader's structure for the collaborators form: a progress field (none, partial, done), the pages read, then pros, cons and bugs, each optional. Let the Feedback button send unsigned feedback too, marked unsigned, so a reader without a key can report a bug from the page it is on. Email stays welcome; the Sherpa logs every message, whichever way it comes.

collaborators/index.html and REALITY.md on 0.8.1.

frictions.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
frictions.actual: Reproduced in every theme and at most widths. The tile 'Websites taken offline' shows '10 organisations' in the 1.35rem serif; 'organisations' is wider than the tile (134 to 142px) and the stylesheet forbids breaking it (.tile b {overflow-wrap: normal}), so it runs 3 to 11px into the next tile. The other tiles fit.
frictions.expected: Put the number alone in the large type ('10') and move the unit into the small line ('organisations took websites offline, as a precaution'), as the other tiles already do with 'Yes' and 'Not yet'. A guard for the next long word: .tile b {overflow-wrap: anywhere}. The gate's browser check could flag any element wider than its tile.

frictions.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
frictions.actual: Reproduced, and it is unreachable by design: the card is drawn with pointer-events: none, it closes as soon as the pointer leaves the word, and 'Open the glossary' is plain text, not a link. The card promises an action it cannot give. Clicking the word itself does open the glossary, but nothing says so. On a touch screen the card cannot be opened at all without following the link.
frictions.expected: Quick and honest: change the line to 'Click the word for the glossary entry'. Proper: make the line a real link to the term's glossary entry, let the card take the pointer (pointer-events: auto) and keep it open for a short grace period while the pointer moves from the word to the card; on touch, the first tap opens the card and the link inside it goes on. Keyboard: focus already opens it; Escape closes it.
evidence: UF-001 point 10, received 2026-10-23

On flaws/index.html on 0.8.1 in Chromium: hovering 'PHP' shows the card (no links inside it, pointer-events none); moving the pointer to 'Open the glossary' closes it. Code: the showTip() and mouseout handler in the site script written by build_sitejs(), and .tip in assets/site.css.
frictions.proposal: Quick and honest: change the line to 'Click the word for the glossary entry'. Proper: make the line a real link to the term's glossary entry, let the card take the pointer (pointer-events: auto) and keep it open for a short grace period while the pointer moves from the word to the card; on touch, the first tap opens the card and the link inside it goes on. Keyboard: focus already opens it; Escape closes it.
